PullRequest.Title: Agents - change the base branch of Branch Changes
PullRequest.Body:

## Why

The Changes picker shows the base branch that Branch Changes compares against (for example "Branch → origin/main", #349442). Users can't change it today. This PR adds the edit experience: a pen right after the base name opens a branch picker. It builds on #350103, which records the base as a full ref and diffs against it exactly.

## What changed

- **Agent Host.** Branch changesets get two operations. `list-base-branches` returns the full refs of every local and remote branch (`refs/heads/main`, `refs/remotes/origin/main`) and the default base ref, as a data result. `set-base-branch` takes the picked ref in `_meta` (`vscode.baseBranchRef`) and records it exactly, in the same folder scope a new session records its base. A ref that isn't a current branch is rejected. Git state then refreshes, which recomputes the diff and `baseBranchRef`.
- **During a turn.** The operation gate allows both operations while a turn runs. They change what the changes are compared against, not the working tree.
- **Shared rendering.** The branch row, the pinned groups, and the list options of the new-session branch picker move to `agentHostBranchPicker.ts`. The new-session picker renders exactly as before.
- **Client.**
  - The provider hides both operations from the buttons and exposes `ISessionChangeset.baseBranchSelection` while the host advertises them.
  - The picker label shows a pen after the base name. It is muted at rest and has its own hover fill. The pen opens the base picker, with groups for the current base, the default branch, and other branches. Rows show `getBaseBranchLabel(ref)` and send the ref.
  - Only the pen opens the branch picker from the label. The label is a `role=button` whose children are presentational, so the pen is pointer-only.
  - The picker opens at once with a "Loading branches…" row and fills in when the branches arrive. A large repository can take over a second to list its branches, and before this the click looked like it did nothing. The filter is always shown, because the list can't add it after it opens.

## Scope

Remote-tracking and local branches only. Tags, commits, and free-form refs are out of scope. Multi-root scopes don't offer base changes: their diff compares every repository against one base, while only the first folder's branches are listed.

## Tradeoffs

- Changing the base resets the reviewed checkmarks, because the review state is keyed by base.
- An existing PR is not retargeted.
- The full branch list is sent at once, with no cap.
- Keyboard and screen reader users have no way to change the base yet.

## Blast radius

The new operations only appear on Branch changesets with a working directory. The rest is the Changes picker label, plus a move-only refactor of the new-session branch picker.

## Verification

- `./scripts/test.sh` with changesViewActions, changesActions, agentHostSessionChangesets and agentHostSessionConfigPicker, after the loading change: 176 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh` with agentHostBaseBranchOperationProvider, agentHostChangesetOperationService, agentHostContributions, changesViewActions, agentHostSessionChangesets, agentHostSessionConfigPicker, changesViewService, sessionChangesEditorInput, agentService and agentHostChangesetCoordinator: 1779 passing, 16 pending.
- Mutation checks:
  - Recording the short name instead of the picked ref fails the set test.
  - Sending the row label instead of its ref fails 2 picker tests.
  - Adding a Change Base Branch row back to the changeset list fails the pen-only test.
  - Waiting for the branches before showing the picker fails the loading test.
  - Dropping the cancel on a new selection fails both stale-selection tests.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run oxlint` on changed files, and `pnpm run valid-layers-check` all pass.
- A live run in the Agents window with a real Agent Host session passed all 7 steps. The pen opens the picker on "Loading branches…" first, then lists the branches with the current base focused. Picking `origin/release/1.0`, then the local `main`, changes the compared files and the label.
- The `sessions/changes/changesPicker` fixtures show the pen at rest, with a custom base, and at a narrow width.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The picker-to-set call path and awaited full query are explicit. getRefs constructs --sort -committerdate, and the Git service documents that this reads every ref's tip commit. Completed reads are not cached. Actual delay depends on branch count and filesystem cache warmth; no timing was measured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: One additional Git subprocess enumerating and sorting all branch refs, reading their tip commits, and buffering/parsing all resulting branch records.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One redundant full-list subprocess per applied selection, not one process per branch. Its work scales with the total number B of local and remote branches: all B refs and tip commits are visited and the records are sorted, even though only one ref is being validated. Same-operation in-flight joining does not help because the picker listing has already completed.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Additional input-size-dependent latency before the selected base is persisted and the comparison refresh can begin.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The base revision had no base-selection operation and did not add this second scan on a picker selection. In the new workflow, the full branch listing is already paid once when opening the picker; repeating that display-oriented query is newly introduced validation work.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Applying one selected ref now waits for another complete, commit-date-sorted branch listing before writing the base metadata and initiating the diff refresh.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new _setBaseBranch implementation awaits getBranches(repositoryRoot, branchQuery) at line 91; branchQuery at line 24 selects every local and remote ref and sorts by committerdate. This adds a second full enumeration after _listBaseBranches has already completed the same query to populate the picker.
Findings.Title: Validate the selected ref without relisting every branch
Findings.Impact: In repositories with thousands of local/remote branches, choosing a base repeats the repository-wide tip-commit reads, sorting, output buffering and parsing, delaying the label and comparison update after the picker closes. Warm filesystem caches reduce I/O latency but do not eliminate the second full scan and sort.
Findings.Evidence: showBaseBranchPicker first awaits getCandidates, then invokes setBaseBranch for a selected row. _listBaseBranches performs getBranches with branchQuery. _setBaseBranch repeats that query solely for branches.some(ref equality). AgentHostGitService.getRefs (lines 183-202) runs git for-each-ref with the query's sort and patterns, and parses the full output. Its in-flight read cache is cleared on completion, so it cannot reuse the listing that produced the selected row. The existing getBranch(repositoryRoot, ref) API (lines 210-230) accepts full refs, performs an unsorted ref-scoped lookup, and selects the exact match.
Findings.Recommendation: Validate the selected full ref with the existing getBranch(repositoryRoot, ref) API and reject an absent or nonmatching result, rather than rerunning the sorted all-branches query. Keep the full sorted query only for populating the picker.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, filter, dismiss, or reopen the new Branch Changes base picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The loading row appears synchronously. Populating selectable rows requires one candidates RPC, repository resolution, the branch query and default-ref resolution, response decoding, row construction and ActionWidget.updateItems. Filtering thereafter is local; dismissal does not await Git.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke list-base-branches on the changeset channel and return the candidate list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical RPC per picker opening; identical concurrent calls on the same operation/channel/credential key join in AgentHostChangesetOperationService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No base picker or candidates RPC existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for actual candidate rows, but not for displaying the loading feedback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On a root-cache miss, check the directory and run git rev-parse --show-toplevel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one root lookup per uncached working directory, with pending lookup joining and a 100-entry LRU including confirmed non-repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This boundary and cache already existed, but there was no base-picker request reaching them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run one full sorted for-each-ref query; resolve the default through remote and symbolic-ref probes and scoped branch lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-list process, not B processes. Default resolution adds a small number of probes: remote -v, origin symbolic-ref, optionally another remote symbolic-ref, and one or two scoped branch lookups; resolving a remote branch can also read remote names.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Git APIs existed; these calls were not made by a Branch Changes base picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both branch listing and default resolution must finish before candidates are returned; they start concurrently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate/copy refs, JSON-stringify and percent-encode a data URI; decode, parse and validate/copy it on the client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One complete O(B)-sized payload per completed listing; no application-level result cap or completed candidate cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before row construction. Client cancellation after the RPC avoids decoding and row construction for a dismissed picker.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: B local and remote branch refs from one repository. Two pinned groups contain at most the current and default refs; remaining row work and response size are O(B).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One listing operation lane per channel/operation; branch enumeration and default resolution run in parallel. When the Git coalescing configuration is enabled, shareable reads use the existing global eight-read limiter; otherwise they run without that limiter. Row DOM remains virtualized, and ActionList avoids all-row width measurement for lists of at least 50 items.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository roots have positive/negative LRU caching and pending joining. Candidate lists have no completed cache. Operation service joins identical in-flight listings. Optional Git read coalescing shares identical pending commands only, not completed output. Reopening after completion queries again. Cancellation prevents stale UI work but does not propagate to the host's CancellationToken.None execution.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced request, operation-lane joining, Git command construction, data-URI conversion, cancellation ownership and ActionList measurement bounds.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Branch counts, remote deployment transport and actual query/parse durations are unmeasured. Full-list loading and linear serialization alone are not reported as bugs; they implement the requested on-demand list.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent high-confidence regression in initial loading, filtering, cleanup or rendering. Full-list loading is intentional and deferred until requested; the separate repeated validation scan is reported under applying a selection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply a selected base branch and update Branch Changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selecting a different row closes the picker, sends set-base-branch, resolves the repository, repeats a complete sorted branch query, then awaits immediate metadata persistence. Only afterward are Git-state and comparison refreshes initiated. The second full branch query therefore directly delays applying the selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke set-base-branch with the selected full ref in metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One operation RPC per different selected ref; selecting the current ref issues none. Identical concurrent operations join; distinct metadata values serialize on the same set-operation lane.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Carries the mutation whose completion precedes updated state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat the complete committer-date-sorted for-each-ref listing solely to test whether one selected ref exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional full-list subprocess per applied selection after the picker listing has completed; visits all B branch tips and buffers/parses all B records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No set operation added this work; the newly added picker has already completed an identical display-oriented listing before a selection is possible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before metadata persistence and before any comparison refresh begins.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the selected folder base to central session state and immediately flush required legacy mirrors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical base metadata write per accepted selection, sequenced per session; cold loading can also read catalog/session state and import required state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same storage machinery and immediate-flush semantics existed for other metadata writers, but no user base-selection write used them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before refresh initiation; immediate mirror completion preserves existing reader compatibility.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh Git status, remote/default facts and base divergence after writing the new base.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Refresh requests are per source/session and same-scope peer chat, but overlapping reads share by working-directory/base-ref, including joining a fresh read. Usually one changed-folder computation plus a separate session-folder computation when different; staggered per-key refreshes can issue later reads. Each computation has a bounded set of repository probes, not one process per branch or changed file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The refresh computation, per-key throttling and shared-read machinery existed, but base-selection did not trigger it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the set-operation response path, but required before the updated Git state drives the comparison UI.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh observed branch comparisons using merge-base/status/diff and optional fingerprint file stats; when untracked files exist, use a temporary index and remove it afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Grouped by observed folder changeset owner, not one full diff per chat. Fingerprint stats cover at most 2,000 changed paths with concurrency 16. Identical owner scheduling/fingerprint reuse bounds repeated recomputation. A plain tracked-file diff uses merge-base, status and diff; the untracked path adds temporary-index setup, staging and cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These comparison and cache mechanisms already existed; the new base-selection action intentionally triggers them with a different baseline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the mutation response path, but required for the selected comparison's files to update.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: B local/remote refs for validation; C chats grouped by effective folder scope for refresh scheduling; one editable repository because multi-root scopes are suppressed; P changed paths for subsequent fingerprints/diffs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Distinct set requests serialize per changeset/operation lane; list and set have separate lanes. Metadata writes serialize per session. Source/session refreshes are requested concurrently and peers independently through per-key five-second throttling, while in-flight Git-state reads coalesce across equal directory/base keys. Optional Git command limiting is global at eight shareable reads. Comparison scheduling is owner-keyed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The picker listing is finished before selection and is not retained by Git's pending-read map, so validation always repeats the full query even with read coalescing enabled. Warm disk caches reduce physical I/O but retain the full enumeration/sort/parse cost. Root and loaded session-state caches normally avoid cold loads. Shared Git-state reads and owner-based diff fingerprints prevent treating every peer refresh as an independent full Git computation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high for the reported extra validation scan: the added awaited query, shared query constant, all-tip sort and lack of completed caching are explicit. Existing getBranch accepts a full ref and selects the exact match without the full sorted listing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings were measured. Severity depends on B and cache warmth; thousands of refs are a realistic scaling trigger. Peer-refresh staggering and optional pending PR reconciliation make total downstream refresh work workload-dependent and are not claimed as per-chat subprocess fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity repeated-work regression at agentHostBaseBranchOperationProvider.ts:91. Use the existing scoped getBranch lookup for validation; retain the full sorted query for populating the picker. No additional finding for intentional persistence or comparison recomputation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the Changes label, resolve shared-folder bases during normal refresh/restore, and use the existing new-session branch picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Changes label reads observable base/availability state and updates existing DOM in place; it does not fetch branches. Existing Git refreshes resolve the authoritative folder base before their Git-state read. The new-session picker continues to obtain its existing completion list before showing options and filters that list locally.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the base from the representative chat/session's persisted folder scope, using a loaded snapshot when available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One base-resolution request per existing refresh. Loaded records use a cached snapshot; unloaded records can read central state/catalog or the legacy scope database. The diff changes which representative resource is read, not the number of logical reads per refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same refresh path already read persisted base state; it selected the individual chat rather than the shared-folder representative.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes the existing Git-state read; unrelated to label rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Obtain the existing new-session local-branch completion list, including current/default branch probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One completion retrieval for a picker opening, with a full local branch listing and a bounded set of branch/default probes; subsequent filtering uses the captured completion list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same local branch query, completion reuse, pinning and filtering behavior; this PR extracts their presentation helpers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing picker-opening path; shared row and list-option helpers do not move this work earlier or increase its call count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: C chats in a session for folder-source selection; B existing new-session local branch completions; a constant-size Changes label and pen.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous work for rendering the label. Existing refresh throttlers and Git-read coalescing still govern persisted-base/Git refreshes. The shared picker helper does no IPC or subprocess work itself.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Label observables do not cause candidate fetching. Base reads reuse cached loaded-session snapshots. Existing new-session filtering reuses branch completions per opening. The newly created pen's listeners/hover are owned by the render store, and picker observers/cancellation sources are disposed on hide or action-item disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: compared the moved helper bodies and list options, traced label observables and disposal stores, and checked shared-scope resolution and session-store cache behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Source selection can scan chat candidates, but no measured material amplification or independently actionable large-session regression was established. Existing completion and persistence costs are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence performance regression. The shared picker code is a presentation extraction; the authoritative-base adjustment does not add a new expensive boundary per refresh.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 21 changed files and their complete diff pages, with targeted caller, cache, Git subprocess, persistence, ActionList rendering and lifecycle tracing. Submitted one introduced repeated-work latency finding for re-enumerating and sorting all branches while validating one selected ref. Rejected unsupported per-chat subprocess-fanout, unbounded DOM rendering, lifecycle leak and correctness-only candidates. No qualifying regression fix with introducing-commit provenance was established. Static read-only review; durations and input prevalence remain unmeasured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
